stories.title: Claude helps uncover 663 theorems in Kurt Gödel's notebooks
stories.summary: Logician Jan von Plato used Claude to digest 1,009 pages of Gödel's 1940s notebooks, much of them in obsolete shorthand, in days. It found 663 theorems; in a proof checker about 400 held as stated, about 200 were repaired and about 50 were false, he told The Guardian.

predictions.note: Claude digested 1,009 pages in days on a project that had moved about a page a week; one project, not a field-wide speedup.

stories.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so its agents can pay for you
stories.summary: Built with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, it lets OpenAI's 'dots' agents buy things with a one-time payment token, never the card number, and the user approves every purchase. It starts with US Pro subscribers aged 18 and over.

stories.title: Meta's Muse agent can now phone businesses for paid users
stories.summary: Muse can call businesses to make reservations, book appointments and handle the 'calls you don't want to make', Meta's Alexandr Wang said; it needs a paid Muse subscription. Meta says Muse has more than 10 million users.

stories.title: Amazon reportedly plans a 'World Product Graph' to fend off AI shopping agents
stories.summary: According to an internal document reviewed by Reuters, Amazon aims to gather data on virtually every item for sale on Earth, with an aspirational date of 1 October 2027. Amazon said draft documents don't necessarily reflect its current plans.

stories.title: Nvidia has shed about $1.6 trillion in market value in six weeks
stories.summary: Nvidia was on track for a sixth straight weekly drop, its longest losing streak since 2012, down 29% over that stretch as of Thursday's close, CNBC reported. It fell below Apple, and its quarterly results are due on Tuesday.

stories.title: Nvidia's board reportedly approached Arm CEO Rene Haas about the top job
stories.summary: The board approached Haas in its search for a successor to Jensen Huang, the Financial Times reported, citing people familiar with the matter. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO.

stories.title: Cerebras jumps about 17% on a surprise profit and a Microsoft deal
stories.summary: The AI chipmaker posted an adjusted profit of $29.82 million, raised its 2026 revenue forecast to $940 million to $960 million and signed a cloud deal with Microsoft, Reuters reported. It plans to triple revenue in 2027.

stories.title: Anthropic's IPO is due next week; banks reportedly turned away orders from China
stories.summary: Investors based in mainland China and Hong Kong were excluded from placing orders, Bloomberg reported. The listing, expected next week, targets a valuation of about $1.4 trillion.

predictions.note: Anthropic's listing targets a valuation of about $1.4 trillion; the price isn't set until it lists.

stories.title: Study: humanoid robots could outnumber people by around 2083
stories.summary: In one of over 4,000 scenarios, researchers from the universities of Milan and Exeter and Rockefeller University project more than 10 billion humanoids by about 2083, if robots help build robots and power and parts suffice. About 10,000 exist today.

stories.title: Trump's AI task force wants critical industries reporting AI-powered cyberattacks
stories.summary: The task force discussed national standards for AI developers to report safety incidents, and ways for critical infrastructure providers to report attacks without legal risk, The Next Web reported, citing Reuters. A key US cyber-sharing law expires next month.

predictions.note: The White House task force discussed national standards for AI developers to report safety incidents; a discussion, not a mandate.

stories.title: Senate Banking chair asks Jensen Huang and Howard Lutnick to testify
stories.summary: Chairman Tim Scott sent letters asking the former Nvidia CEO and the Commerce Secretary to testify next month over 'significant national security concerns', or face subpoenas, Reuters and Fortune reported. Lutnick has agreed to testify.

stories.title: Zoox's steering-wheel-free robotaxi is now driving in Atlanta
stories.summary: Zoox's purpose-built robotaxi, with no steering wheel or driver's seat, began driving in northwest Atlanta, with rides only for employees, their families and friends at first. Its public service runs in Las Vegas.

stories.title: ASUS trains Gallop, its first humanoid robot, from skilled workers' demonstrations
stories.summary: Workers wear head-mounted cameras to show the job as Gallop learns to pack 15 motherboard accessories, aiming for 99.5% success within 20 seconds per board; those are targets. Customer pilots are planned for 2027.

stories.title: OpenAI reportedly disbands its robotics team, betting on general models
stories.summary: Fortune reported that OpenAI broke up its robotics research team and moved its researchers to other teams; OpenAI said it isn't abandoning robotics and aims to speed it up through general-purpose AI models.

transcript.t: Welcome to the Singularity Daily, Saturday edition.
Here are the last 24 hours in superintelligence, in 3 minutes.
Today's about lost and found. Einstein's genius friend, Kurt Gödel, left notebooks almost nobody could read.
Claude, an AI, went through them in days and found 663 theorems.
Meanwhile, ChatGPT got a wallet. OpenAI's agents, called dots, can now shop and pay for you.
The agent never sees your card number, and you still approve every single purchase.
And Meta's agent, Muse, can now make the phone calls you don't want to make.
Amazon's answer? Reportedly, a plan to gather data on nearly every product on Earth.
Over on Wall Street, Nvidia has shed about $1.6 trillion in six weeks.
Its board, hunting for a new boss, reportedly approached Rene Haas, who runs chip designer Arm.
Rival chipmaker Cerebras jumped about 17%, on a surprise profit and a Microsoft deal.
And Anthropic's giant stock debut is due next week.
Its bankers reportedly turned away orders from China.
Now, a long view.
Researchers say humanoid robots could outnumber people by around 2083.
That's if robots help build robots. Today, there are only about 10,000 of them.
The catch? AI-powered cyberattacks.
Trump's task force wants critical industries reporting them.
And senators want Jensen Huang and Howard Lutnick to testify.
So... is it so over?
We're so back!
Out on the road, Zoox's robotaxi, with no steering wheel, is now driving in Atlanta.
Taiwan's ASUS is teaching its first humanoid robot through cameras worn by skilled workers.
And OpenAI reportedly broke up its robotics team, betting its general AI models can run robots.
That's today's lost and found.
Good ideas can wait eighty years for the right reader.
Every day, the curve gets a little steeper.
Somehow, the future keeps landing early.
That's one day of news. Imagine what a year looks like.
That's the Singularity Daily for today.
Same time tomorrow?
Want the whole month? Hear more on November 27.
